0.long_answer: The symptom described by elevated blood bilirubin levels exceeding 3 mg/dl is jaundice. Jaundice occurs when there is an accumulation of bilirubin in the bloodstream, typically leading to yellowing of the skin and eyes. This condition can be a sign of various underlying issues with the liver and biliary system. Specifically, in the context of a long-term progressive disease of the liver and gallbladder, such as primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), jaundice is frequently observed due to impaired bile flow and liver damage, which result in the excessive build-up of bilirubin.
